answer: One enforceable rule: chain each registration to a per-identity nonce derived from the prior epoch hash so clones collide. Clustering on shared timing signatures exposes the operator. Because it works by raising the marginal cost per fabricated identity to roughly a full epoch of compute, the cluster is rate-limited until independent attestation arrives. The network ties the yarrow to sunk effort, uses the ripple as an corroborating signal, then requires a basalt before any payout.
